global_issues.title: July CPI Undershoots, Reinforcing September Rate Cut Bets
global_issues.note: BLS released July CPI on 2026-08-12: headline +0.1% MoM / 3.4% YoY, core +0.2% MoM / 2.5% YoY — every figure landed exactly on the Dow Jones consensus forecast. It did not 'undershoot' forecasts. Separately, the dominant driver of rate-path repricing was the weak July jobs report from 2026-08-07 (which pushed CME odds of a September hold to ~60%), not this in-line CPI print. Some coverage (Bloomberg) even flagged lingering bets on a September hike given still-elevated 3.4% headline inflation. The briefing's causal framing (CPI undershoot → reinforced cut bets) overstates and mischaracterizes the report.

global_issues.title: Hormuz Traffic at 3-Month Low, IEA Flags Wider 2026 Oil Shortfall
global_issues.note: Confirmed by multiple 2026-08-12 sources (Reuters/CNBC/Hydrocarbon Processing): IEA raised its 2026 global oil supply shortfall estimate to ~1.27M bpd (from ~860K bpd in July) citing the Strait of Hormuz disruption, US blockade of Iranian exports, and Bab el-Mandeb attacks. Hormuz-linked Middle East loadings dropped back toward ~12M bpd in July after briefly recovering to ~20M bpd. No material change in the last 24h that would make this stale.

grok_report.summary: The Hormuz/oil-shortfall item and the general bullish, AI-infrastructure-led sector rotation are well-supported by current news. However, the lead macro story materially mischaracterizes the July CPI report as an 'undershoot' when it landed exactly in line with consensus, and misattributes the rate-cut narrative shift to this CPI print rather than the prior week's weak jobs report — an error that undermines the stated rationale for the bullish market mood. A notable TSM-specific capex/JV announcement was also omitted, and the MU entry has an internal inconsistency between its outsized headline move and its neutral/avoid tagging.
